Great — based on our earlier conversation about Strats, Les Pauls, open-D tuning and coil-splitting, here are some focused things to check for when you try guitars at the shop:

- Body/neck feel: compare the Strat and Les Paul shapes and neck joints. The Strat has a contoured, bolt-on body; the Les Paul is single-cut with a set neck and a thicker (often mahogany + maple) body. Pick the shape and neck profile that feels best in your hands.

- Pickups and tonal options: listen to the pickup voices. If you like more tonal flexibility, try a Les Paul with coil-tap / coil-splitting (it gives you more single-coil–like tones in addition to humbucker warmth).

- Playability and setup: pay attention to string action and fretboard comfort. For lower tunings (like open D) heavier strings and a proper setup give fuller, more resonant tone — try heavier gauges if the shop has them.

- Amp and settings: plug into an amp and try different amp settings and pickup positions to hear how the guitar sits in clean and driven tones (this matters especially for Les Pauls, which excel at warm, sustaining rock tones).

- What you’ll play: bring something you know well (chords, riffs, fingerpicking bits) so you can compare how each guitar responds to your usual techniques.

- Coil-split test: if the guitar has coil-split/tap, switch it on and off while playing to hear the difference — it can be a big reason to choose one instrument over another.

Try several instruments, compare feel and tone, and pick the one that inspires you to play. Have a great time at the store this weekend!
